READ FIRST
- ALL of $SP/v2/WAVE3.md, the wave-3 design. It is authoritative together with the owner's words:
  - §3 data contracts; §4 runtime; §5 budgets; §6 responsible design (hard rules);
  - §7 voices; §8 gestures; §9 variety; §10 ownership and hub rules.

  - the latest section of every module you touch or consume;
  - the "wave-3 architect" pointer and the "wave-3 hub edit log".
- docs/programmes/*.md, the style bibles. Wave 3 replaces only their running times and story counts; their voice, camera, set, graphics and tone rules still hold.

WHAT THE OWNER SAID (translated)
- "If the programme ends in 3 minutes we have nothing."
  - Programmes must be MUCH longer, with more possibilities.
  - Still produced LIVE by the server a few minutes ahead, never pre-planned.
- Many more slides, driven only by episode data.
- 23:00, interviews: "use REAL ones, just to make them closer: the person appears on the screen or in the studio."
  - They voice ONLY their sourced words.
  - Labelled "RECREATION — WORDS FROM PUBLIC STATEMENTS".
- 23:05: "Don't forget the EXPERTS — that brings the programme to life."
  - The channel's own recurring analysts and correspondents.
  - They speak strictly within the facts.
- Voices: "take the step to the next level: more natural, even if it still sounds artificial — e.g. laughs etc. (without exaggerating)".
- Hands: "make sure they DON'T OVERUSE them".
- Always: adult (NEVER a children's programme), pixel craft ("nothing drawn with triangles, squares and circles"), real polish, a calm 24/7 pace.

YOUR JOB
Today the server makes a whole 2-minute episode in one AI call. Wave 3 needs:
- 9-26 minute blocks;
- produced in PARTS: part 1 airs while later parts are written, reviewed, illustrated and voiced;
- the queue kept a target number of minutes ahead of air;
- deadlines, budgets and graceful fallbacks, so the channel never stalls.
Read server/station.js, producer.js, providers/*, news.js, images.js, voice/service.js and director.js first. Station.fill/advance, the provider chain with cooldowns, the picture desk and the voice stage already exist.

YOU OWN
See owns. server/producer.js is a hub you own.

CONTRACTS YOU IMPLEMENT (WAVE3.md)
- §3.1 dossier.
- §3.3 block shell, Part, and the endpoints:
  - GET /api/next (shell + back-compat segments);
  - GET /api/episode/:id/part/:n?wait=20&playing=m (200 / 202 {state, eta} / 410 dropped / 404);
  - GET /api/episode/:id (loopback/dev);
  - SSE 'part' events;
  - /api/status.production { lead, voiceLead, budget, tasks, fallbacks }.
- §3.8 AI stages: plan (merged with part 1 by default), part, review (risk-based), book.
- §4 scheduler, deadlines and fallbacks.
- §5 budgets and light mode.
- §1 soft clock.

DELIVERABLES (in this order)
1. DAY ONE, so w3-air can start:
   - Serve today's single-shot episode as a block whose parts are split at story boundaries (2 parts; NEWS IN 60 1 part).
   - The shell carries parts, guests {}, outro.safe (today's outro) and the back-compat segments.
   - The part endpoint long-polls with a timeout and records the 'playing' playhead.
   - Tests. A CONTRACTS section with exact JSON examples.
2. DOSSIERS (server/production/dossier.js + news.js):
   - The article page fetched for pictures also yields the body text: readability-lite; drop nav, aside, footer, related and boilerplate; cleaned paragraphs; ≤ 4,000 chars.
   - Local fixture pages are read through the existing local-page path.
   - Same-event outlets come from the existing sameEvent cluster.
   - Compute the depth score; text ≤ 9,000 chars.
   - Run within dossierBudgetMs (default 8000) next to the picture desk. Late pages keep resolving for later parts.
   - Keep the existing fetch guards: private IPs, maxBytes, timeouts.
   - Then call w3-guests' extractQuotes(story) when it exists, to fill story.quotes.
3. BLOCK PRODUCTION (server/production/blocks.js, parts.js, producer.js):
   - Producer.produceBlock(channel, programId, { targetSec, clock, upcoming }):
     a. candidates + dossiers + quotes;
     b. the PLAN(+P1) stage through w3-format normalizePlan;
     c. bookGuests (w3-guests);
     d. parts as scheduler tasks.
   - Each part runs: write (normalizePart) → review (risk-based: always on parts with quote segments, guest lines, the lead, or figures in visuals; elsewhere only if the budget allows) → assets → voice.
   - Assets verify pictures, including up to 3 per story for gallery and photo slides: /api/img/<id>?n=k plus a verified list on the story.
   - Keep markCovered/markOffered and recentLines semantics per block.
   - NEWS IN 60 is a 1-part block through the same machinery. The old produce() stays as a thin wrapper while tests migrate.
4. SCHEDULER (server/production/scheduler.js):
   - Tasks: PLAN, WRITE, REVIEW, BOOK, ASSETS, VOICE.
   - Deadlines come from estimated air times: the block start, the parts' estimated durations (w3-format estimate.js, or voice durations once rendered) and the client's 'playing' reports.
   - Earliest deadline first across blocks.
   - Per-provider lanes: codex is serial; openai-compatible providers may run N in parallel (config).
   - Never start a WRITE before air − AHEAD_MAX_S (1500), unless lead < LEAD_TARGET_S and the lane is idle.
   - Lead accounting: LEAD_TARGET_S 600, LEAD_MIN_S 240. Voice lead target is 120 s.
   - Deadline misses:
     - WRITE → writePartDeterministic (w3-demo) for that part; a late AI answer is discarded and logged;
     - PLAN → planDeterministic;
     - REVIEW → skipped, part.reviewed=false (deterministic checks always ran);
     - BOOK → generic booking;
     - VOICE → late clips attach in place, as today.
   - Optional parts that cannot make it are 'dropped'.
   - ProviderChain.generate(request, validate, { deadline, signal }) aborts at the deadline. codexExec kills its child process; openaiCompat uses an AbortSignal. Keep the cooldowns.
5. BUDGET (server/production/budget.js):
   - AI_CALLS_PER_HOUR (default 24); AI busy share ≤ 60 %; tokens per day; projection for the next hour from the clock.
   - Light-mode levels per WAVE3 §5, in order, logged once per transition.
   - Voice RTF measured from voice notes.
   - usage.js records per stage.
   - All of it shown in /api/status.production.
6. SOFT CLOCK (config/schedule.json + clock.js):
   - The fixed points of WAVE3 §1 (NEWS IN 60 at :00 and :30 London), dayparts (overnight light edition, weekend WEEK IN REVIEW flag), rotation fallback when off.
   - The station picks the next programme from the clock and gives the plan targetSec.
   - It drops optional parts late, and stretches or shrinks breaks (breakItem ads count, filler), to land fixed points within ±90 s.
   - schedule() and upNext reflect it, for the on-screen schedule.
   - Skip a slot whose programme cannot be produced: canProduce and IN THEIR WORDS' material requirement.
7. Aired-story ARCHIVE: data/archive.jsonl, 8 days, archive.recent(days). Consumed by w3-format for WEEK IN REVIEW.
8. BREAKING NEWS MID-BLOCK: a new breaking story is passed to the next unwritten part's task input (part.breaking = storyId).
9. FIXTURE MODE (local FEEDS_FILE): COVERED_TTL_H (default 3), so the offline demo can run all day. Real feeds keep today's rules.
10. STRETCH: snapshot the queue and blocks to data/station.json and restore them on restart.
11. LAB public/lab/w3-production.html:
    - a 384x216 #screen canvas drawing the production timeline: blocks, parts with states (planned / producing / ready / dropped / fallback), deadlines, the playhead, the lead bar and budget gauges;
    - live from /api/status.production;
    - __lab.render(t) replays a recorded status log deterministically (fixture), for shoot.mjs;
    - calm, readable, in the channel style.

TESTS (test/w3-produce.test.js, plus updates to the existing ones)
- The parts API: 200/202/410/404, long-poll with a fake clock, the playing playhead, back-compat segments.
- EDF ordering across two blocks.
- A deadline miss on a slow fake provider → the deterministic writer is used and the late answer discarded.
- Review skipped by budget.
- BOOK late → generic booking.
- Lead accounting.
- AHEAD_MAX respected.
- Optional part dropped late.
- Breaking insertion.
- Budget projection and light-mode levels.
- Clock landing within ±90 s over a 6 h simulation (sim.js with the mock).
- Dossier extraction on fixture pages: body, cluster, depth.
- Gallery images verified.
- Fixture coverage TTL.
- The existing station, producer, server and news tests stay green, or are migrated with the reason.

ACCEPTANCE (measured)
- Offline demo:
  - blocks with parts appear;
  - curl shows the shell and parts;
  - within 5 minutes /api/status.production shows lead ≥ 600 s with the mock;
  - with MOCK_DELAY_MS=90000 the lead stays ≥ 240 s and fallbacks are reported, never a stall.
- The 6 h simulation report (blocks per programme within WAVE3 §1 ranges, clock error, lead minimum, fallbacks, calls per hour vs budget) is saved under $SP/shots/w3-produce/sim/.
- Lab sheets of the production timeline.

RULES
- Ownership:
  - edit ONLY the files you own, plus the surgical hub edits listed in hubEdits;
  - for a hub edit: re-read the file right before, make the smallest diff, never reformat, and log it in CONTRACTS "wave-3 hub edit log";
  - never run git commands that change state;
  - if you need something in another stream's file, write a Request in CONTRACTS ("FROM w3-produce TO <stream>: ...") and work around it meanwhile.
- Ports: yours is 8701; critics use 8801 and 8901.

  - Open http://127.0.0.1:8701/?autostart=1&voice=mute (add &v2=1 only if v2 is not yet the default).
  - Kill your servers when done.
- Visual work is judged by LOOKING at frames:
  - capture with node tools/shoot.mjs;
  - deterministic lab captures ALWAYS use ?still=1 with --step "window.__lab.render(T)";

- Tests:
  - run your own test files plus test/cues, test/writer and test/providers (and test/speechtext if you touch cues or voice text);
  - run the full node --test once at the end;
  - if test/codexExec.test.js fails under load, re-run it alone and report both results;
  - report failures in areas you do not own; never "fix" them.
- Code style: ES modules, 2-space indent, single quotes, semicolons, a short header comment per module, comments that explain why. English in code and UI.
- CONTRACTS: append your API section ("## 2026-10-0x w3-produce: ...") as soon as it is stable, and update it when it changes.

FINAL REPORT
- Files changed, with hub edits listed precisely.
- What a viewer or operator now sees.
- The 2-4 most representative sheet.png absolute paths.
- Measured numbers.
- Requests still open.
- What is still weak.
Never claim something works unless you saw it in a frame, a log or a test.

critics.lens: Channel operator / master-control lens: would this keep a 24/7 channel on air for days with a slow serial AI and a busy CPU? Lead target honoured, deadlines realistic, fallbacks invisible to viewers (no stalls, no broken promises, no repeated content), clock landing at :00/:30, budgets respected and visible, logs readable. Judge it by the 6 h simulation and the offline demo, not by the code's intentions.

Technical check: scheduler correctness (EDF, lanes, abort at deadline, no leaked timers or child processes), parts API semantics and back-compat for old clients, dossier fetch security (private IPs, size and time limits), determinism of the simulation, budget accounting, tests meaningful and green, ownership respected (no edits outside owns except logged hub edits).
